correctness.rationale: The exact coalescing dual maps each fixed-age spin-pair covariance to the hitting probability of a rate-two separation walk. Equilibrium Pareto age has correctly normalized survival H. The exact walk Laplace transform q(s)^n admits a Mellin-to-Beta integral, yielding the explicit negative hitting-time moment for n>b. The Pareto tail of H matches c t^-b; a Poisson jump-count bound and the 2b negative moment make the short-age cutoff correction superpolynomial. Gamma asymptotics, power-series summability, and a weighted covariance identity prove the spatial prefactor, alpha=3/2 susceptibility threshold, and three block-variance constants. The alpha<=1 supplement follows from renewal age divergence and recurrent coalescence for finite collections. The extracted finite verifier successfully ran 71 independent numerical and analytical-identity checks; they do not substitute for universal proof.

originality.rationale: The verified primary Pareto-reset Ising paper provides a spatially averaged magnetization/renewal analysis, not the zero-temperature annealed spatial pair covariance, exact coalescence Mellin identity, exponent coefficient, susceptibility threshold, or block variance trichotomy. A closely relevant voter-model paper analyzes independent Poisson resetting per site rather than a common Pareto renewal. Published classical duality and Poisson-reset analyses are acknowledged as antecedents. Direct comparisons against accessible related texts and targeted semantic record searches reveal no known result that implies the entire stated model-specific classification; this is qualified originality, not a proof of global uniqueness.
residual_risks: An unlocated broad renewal/coalescing-walk or Tauberian theorem could imply the spatial power exponent or even its coefficient; no exhaustive publication-priority guarantee is possible.
The earlier global-Poisson Ising work was compared at abstract and cited-model level, not exhaustively at its full-text theorem level.
The infinite-mean renewal boundary uses a standard infinite-mean nonlattice renewal theorem; it is not claimed as a new renewal theorem.
Independent correctness and publication-priority audit have not been performed.

value.rationale: A Pareto common reset clock transforms diffusive coarsening into a continuum of exactly normalized stationary spatial power laws. The threshold at alpha=3/2 separates spatially summable correlations from non-summable ones even though stationary renewal age already exists at alpha>1; it induces sharp anomalous, logarithmically corrected, and ordinary self-averaging regimes. These are physically natural equal-time observables, not a parameter renaming, a known table recalculation, or an unsupported minor gain. The exact hitting-time Gamma identity and controlled renewal cutoff make this a reusable benchmark.
